items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I always loved Louis... I practiced Louis Armstrong solos... started me listening to Louis again... enjoying the music of Louis a little bit more.

ctx.x: There’s a lot of music in college that you won’t play anywhere else, because the music just takes so long to prepare. In other words, not to get on another tangent, it’s about time when you get in a professional arena, if you go to the Chicago Symphony, well let me give a better example. When you go play a show somewhere, they’re going to try and make the music not so difficult because they might have an hour, two hours at the most, to rehearse it. They can’t give you a bunch of incredibly hard stuff, they’re…

items.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 25, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: You saw and sat next to Freddie Hubbard and played with him. Just go down the list. That’s what they’re looking for.” ... “You didn’t see Louis.

ctx.x: Well I had to do almost the exact same scenario and some of the students seem to work well in the format and others didn’t and I wondered just how do you motivate them?

Right. So good question. What I was saying is, where I was going with that is I felt also I began each lesson with five, ten minutes max if I could, just, how are you feeling? How is this affecting you? Because that’s going to affect how you play, your desire to practice and everything. Some kids were isolated. They hadn’t left — they were scared to leave their room — some kids I had to say maybe you don’t need to go out as often. You know? So everybody was dealing with a mental thing. So I thought it was good to…

each particular — what got each particular student energized and motivated. And so a quick aside to that is for young people I’ve been finding, maybe you found this, that if the person is living then they’re more apt to be attracted to it. I don’t know if you’ve gotten that. So check it out. So I’ll tell somebody hey, bring — I want to have them do what they want to do first. I say, “Bring in a transcribed solo, anybody you want to, let’s work on it next week.
